summary.headline: K.P. Energy FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,500 crore (up 57% YoY) and Q4 PAT hit a record INR 78.69 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 consolidated total revenue of INR 1,505.54 crore (up 57% YoY), EBITDA of INR 328.44 crore (up 68%) and PAT of INR 181.4 crore (up 57%). Q4 net sales reached an all-time quarterly high of INR 631.81 crore, up 83% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 21% (up 194 bps YoY) and PAT of INR 78.69 crore. The order book is about 2 GW (INR 3,000 plus crore), with about 230 MW added in Q4, while operating cash flow weakened due to higher inventory (WTG turbines) and advances. Management guided to 40-50% growth in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +83% QoQ from INR 344.96 crore in Q3 FY26; all-time quarterly high
+71% YoY; margin 21% vs 19% in Q4 FY25 (+194 bps)
+72% YoY from INR 45.79 crore; highest ever quarterly PAT

segments.name: EPC and infrastructure development
segments.commentary: Core engine at INR 1,451.69 crore in FY26 (+59% YoY). Order book of about 2 GW valued at roughly INR 3,000 crore, about 50% from Group entities.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 5.13 crore (+350% YoY); manages over 646 MW under O&M, supported by a 24x7 NOC using IBM Maximo-based AI alerts and SCADA dashboards.

segments.name: IPP
segments.commentary: Operational portfolio of 48.5 MW at year-end; a further 200 MW of IPP capacity is under development (two 100 MW projects). Q4 IPP revenue declined YoY on marginally lower wind performance, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth guidance of 40-50%, which management said is backed by sufficient orders in hand.
Scale EPC execution to convert the near 2 GW order book into revenue; majority of current order book expected to be completed by FY27.
Long-term target of 10 GW total portfolio by 2030; current renewable portfolio exceeds 3.7 GW and projects in hand exceed 2.1 GW.

IPP projects of 200 MW: estimated project cost about INR 1,700 crore plus, with about INR 450 crore plus equity and the balance debt; timeline 24 months from PPA (first PPA window 15 April 2026 to 15 April 2028).
Expected debt cost for upcoming IPP projects of 7.5% to 8.5%.
CERC interstate power trading licence received; management sees no working capital stretch as power trading payments are made in advance.
capex_capacity: IPP operational portfolio of 48.5 MW at year-end, with 200 MW pipeline under development in two 100 MW projects.
Turbine pre-booking and reservation done in advance to secure supply; company is carrying WTG inventory for upcoming projects.
Make-in-India 4.2 MW, 160 m wind turbine installed in South Gujarat, described as the first in India.

Offshore wind and PSP (pumped storage) being evaluated; India's offshore plan is 30 GW by 2030 with initial 4 GW bids off Gujarat and Tamil Nadu. Management said the segment is at a nascent stage and it awaits central policy and VGF clarity.
demand_pricing: Order book about 2 GW / INR 3,000 plus crore; about 230 MW (INR 730 plus crore excluding GST) of new orders added in Q4 FY26.
Pipeline of INR 3,000 plus crore is entirely non-Group; Group orders enter only the order book.
Management cited India FY26 wind additions of 6.05 GW (record) and cumulative wind of over 56 GW; government target of 140 GW by 2030.
Margin commentary: EPC contracts with turbine supply carry a smaller margin than EPC-only contracts, per management.
Power sales from IPP were 6.18 (Q3) and 5.62 (Q4), per management, which it said was a nominal change.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow fall sharply versus last year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Shabana Belim attributed it to a rise in inventory (WTG turbines) ahead of upcoming projects, amid geopolitical supply risk; debtors were broadly stable relative to revenue growth. Cash conversion cycle ranges from 100 to 150 days depending on customer.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital normalise once the geopolitical situation settles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital will stay higher in proportion to 55% revenue growth plus upcoming order mobilisation; higher inventory will convert into debtors over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 gross margin typically lower and how do turbine-included EPC margins compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs were in line with prior periods and EBITDA margin improved to 21.82% in FY26 from 20.46% in FY25; turbine-inclusive EPC contracts carry a somewhat lower margin than EPC-only contracts because of pre-booked turbine leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did IPP unit generation and revenue decline in Q4 YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a marginal decline in wind performance in Q4 and described it as seasonal, with no concern on operating assets.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the order book is Group versus non-Group, and when will it be executed?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of the INR 3,000 plus crore order book is from Group entities; the pipeline excludes Group entities. Majority of current orders expected to complete by FY27, with more additions expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the CERC trading licence and its revenue timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited India's FY25 short-term trading of about 230 BU out of 1,830 BU generated and IEX FY26 volume of 141 BU (up about 17%); no timeline or revenue figure was given.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow weakness: inventory build and mobilisation costs; debt funding need for 200 MW IPP (about INR 1,250 crore debt at 7.5-8.5%).
Cash conversion cycle of 100-150 days, with working capital likely to stay elevated.
Execution risk in converting about 2 GW order book by FY27 and the 40-50% growth target.
IPP generation seasonality and wind performance (Q4 IPP revenue down YoY).
Offshore wind and VGF policy still nascent; no firm project timeline.
Group-entity concentration: about 50% of the order book is from Group entities.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, order flow and the wind demand outlook. Cautious and somewhat evasive on operating cash flow, inventory and working-capital questions, which management attributed to supply-chain and geopolitical factors, and vague on offshore wind and trading-licence revenue timing.
key_quotes: As we step into FY26-27, our priorities are defined and our conviction in the sector has never been stronger than before.
That sequential acceleration is a particularly strong signal of execution velocity that we build specifically through the second half of the year.
